external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who sign in through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are employees, contractors, or another category.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: People from franchise stores who authenticate through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: own devices at home
external_entities.description: Devices colleagues use to sign in from home.
external_entities.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: System that supplies group-membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated by the franchise side that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: franchise stores
external_entities.description: Stores against which the store admin console can operate.
external_entities.source_excerpt: so a store-manager token works against every store

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Broker that signs colleagues in, issues tokens, consumes HR changes, accepts franchise identity-provider sign-ins, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: applications
processes.description: Applications that consume broker-issued tokens and decide what colleagues may do from the groups in the token.
processes.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: Application that lets a holder with the store-manager group change prices and void transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: Store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state where the key store runs or whether it is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: Log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The text does not state whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues sign in through the identity broker using their own identity provider's vouching.
data_flows.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues tokens for applications to use.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker-issued token is consumed by the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: Applications fetch the public half of the signing key from the identity broker to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.

data_flows.name: use signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker uses the signing key kept in the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls group-membership changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains the directory with colleagues and their group memberships.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_flows.notes: Group membership is supplied from the HR system overnight.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down whether the log covers the franchise route or what it records.

data_flows.name: change prices and void transactions
data_flows.description: The store admin console changes prices and voids transactions against every store when the token has the store-manager group.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: own devices at home
trust_boundaries.description: Franchise or colleague-owned home-device zone from which colleagues sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: Zone controlled by the franchise stores and containing franchise colleagues and stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker is a non-web process because the source describes it as a broker rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it an identity broker; the interface-kind rule treats a broker as non-web.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source names it a console, which is treated as a web application interface under the interface-kind rule.

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker is internally exposed rather than internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly places it on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console is internally exposed rather than internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly places it on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds a token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds a signing key; signing keys are secrets.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it holds colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory holds colleagues and their group memberships, which are personal information.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's contents are confidential because it records sign-ins associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log; sign-in records are personal information.
